Raise / reaffirm / cut read on the FY26 guide: RAISE, high confidence. 9M26 revenue of NT$3,898.73bn is +41.1% YoY
[5], and 4Q26 quarterly consensus of NT$1,613.09bn [1] on top of that implies approx. +44.7% FY26 growth in TWD."Slightly above 40%" in USD was set on 2026-07-16 before three consecutive monthly records; with Q3 landing above
the guide's own ceiling, reaffirming "slightly above 40%" would be a deliberate sandbag rather than a forecast. Themechanism is also intact on management's own description: AI demand "extremely robust", cloud customers and
customers' customers giving "very strong signal", and the newly flagged agentic-AI CPU resurgence adding silicon
demand on top of accelerators across x86, ARM and RISC-V — "they are almost all TSMC's customers" [111]. Against
that, management explicitly reserved caution for the consumer and price-sensitive end markets, "challenged due tothe impact of rising component prices and macroeconomics uncertainties", and said it is "being prudent in our business
planning" [111] — the one sentence a bear can hold onto.SBC: not a material line for TSMC and not a non-GAAP bridge item — the company guides and reports on IFRS and
publishes no adjusted-EPS measure, so there is no non-GAAP/GAAP gap to flag. The corollary matters for §6: TSMC
issues no EPS guidance, so "beat vs own guide" can only be measured on revenue and margin.
3. Key Debates from the Last Call
Debate 1: Is the N2 + overseas-fab margin dilution a two-quarter air pocket or a multi-year reset of the margin ceiling?
The debate: TSMC guided gross margin down approx. 1.7pp sequentially even as revenue stepped up 12% — can the
company hold a mid-60s gross margin through the steepest node ramp and the largest overseas build-out in itshistory?
Bull view: The dilution is mechanical and front-loaded. N2 was just 3% of wafer revenue in 2Q26 [119]; yields and
overhead absorption improve every quarter from here, and management named the offsets — "very strong demandfor our leading-edge technologies and continued cost improvement efforts, including productivity gains and across-
node capacity optimization" [109]. Pricing is the other lever: reported 3–6% wafer price increases effective January
2027 would land just as N2 dilution peaks [53][16]. 2Q26 gross margin of 67.7% came in above guidance on costimprovement and utilization [78].
Bear view: The drags stack rather than offset. Management quantified N2 dilution at 3–4pp for all of 2H26 andsimultaneously reiterated overseas dilution of 2–3pp "in the early stages", widening to 3–4pp in the latter stages over
the next several years [109]. With 12 planned US facilities and approx. 30% of leading-edge N2-and-beyond capacity
eventually in Arizona [78], plus a potential Texas campus [86][84], the overseas mix only grows. Add "we have nocontrol over the foreign exchange rate" [109] and the 65-67% guide starts to look like the new normal rather than a
trough.What the last print showed: 2Q26 gross margin 67.7%, operating margin 60.3%, net margin 55.6% on revenue of
$40.20bn / NT$1,270.38bn [78] — a sequential gross-margin gain of 150bp driven by cost work and utilization, partly
offset by overseas-fab dilution [109]. FactSet-computed gross margin has risen from 51.7% in 2Q24 to 66.7% in 2Q26[23], i.e. the structural trend has been up through the entire build-out so far.
Status into this print: leaning bull, but unresolved. Revenue came in 2.4% above the TWD-equivalent guidemidpoint [3][13] with FX at the assumption — operating leverage on unguided volume should push margins toward the
upper half of the range. The genuine unknown is the 4Q26 margin guide, which is the first quarter to carry a full N2
quarter plus incremental Arizona ramp.
Debate 2: How much more capex, and does the capital-intensity step-up break thereturns story?
The debate: Capex has been raised twice in 2026 — $52–56bn in January, "closer to $56bn" in April, $60–64bn now
[110]. Analysts pressed four separate times for a multi-year number and did not get one.
Bull view: Capex is demand-pull, not speculative. Management's framing is explicit: "a higher level of capitalexpenditures is always correlated to higher growth opportunities in the following years" [110], and on the driver of the
raise, "demand continue to increase and we feel the pressure from the customer... for the capacity increase" [115]. Thethree-year capex statement was upgraded mid-sentence from "significantly higher" to "even more significantly higher
than the past three years" [112]. Demand still exceeds supply by what the CEO would only characterize as "a very big
gap" [118]. No bottleneck is foreseen because tool suppliers are engaged years ahead [110].
Bear view: Part of the increase is price, not capacity — "the second reason is inflation. Now, we buy the tools with the
inflation price" [115], and separately TSMC and ASML are reported to be in a cycle of equipment price increases [53].Deputy Co-COO Cliff Hou has said the company has had to roughly double planned equipment purchases over the
past year [84]. If a chunk of the $8bn raise buys the same wafers at a higher price, incremental ROIC degrades,depreciation steps up into 2027–28, and the gross-margin reset in Debate 1 becomes permanent. Management also
declined to break out advanced packaging capex separately despite being asked to — "we cannot very specifically
say which area we put how much of the CapEx" [110].What the last print showed: 2Q26 capex of NT$496bn / US$15.7bn, against NT$783bn of operating cash flow [119]
— the spend is still internally funded with room to spare, and the cash balance rose NT$99bn to NT$3.1tn in thequarter with NT$3.5tn / $110bn of cash and marketable securities [119].
Status into this print: unresolved, and the single highest-variance item. Sell-side is now at $85bn (2027E) and
$98bn (2028E) [6]. Any 2027 capex frame on the call — even a range — immediately re-rates the whole WFEcomplex, and ASML reports the day before [63].
Debate 3: Will TSMC monetize the shortage through price, and how is it being valuedagainst memory?
The debate: Memory peers are earning extraordinary margins off the same AI shortage. Gokul Hariharan asked
directly whether TSMC's foundry role deserves better long-term profitability and what pricing approach it would take.Bull view: TSMC has the pricing power and is beginning to use it. Reports point to 3–6% wafer price increases from
January 2027 on N2/N3, approx. 5% blended, hitting Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm and Apple [53][52][16].Order visibility on mature nodes reportedly extends toward 2030 [52]. TSMC held 72.5% of the foundry market in
2Q26 per TrendForce [82]; no customer has an alternative at N2.
Bear view: Management has pre-committed itself against opportunistic pricing: "we don't suddenly increase our priceby which I like to have, 4x or 5x" — the customer "got to be successful... I don't want to squeeze them out from the
market" [113]. That is a deliberate choice to leave value on the table, and Wei said so almost explicitly in the sameanswer when he compared TSMC's margin to memory's and conceded he would not be happy at 68% [113]. The read-
through: TSMC's margin ceiling is a policy variable set below the economic maximum, which caps the re-rating a
shortage can deliver.What the last print showed: No price action was announced or confirmed; the 3Q26 guide carried no pricing
commentary beyond cost improvement and mix [109]. Mature-node tightness was described as narrow, not broad —only AI-adjacent mature nodes (power management IC at 0.18µm/90nm, sensors) are short, while "the consumer
product is not in a high demand" and other segments are "not so much of, say, in a lot of shortage. Not at all" [115].
Status into this print: leaning bull on realization, leaning bear on magnitude. Expect the question to be asked againon 10-15; expect management to decline to confirm specifics, as it has done for every pricing question to date. Any
confirmation of a 2027 price increase is a clear positive for 2027 consensus margins.
Debate 4: Customer concentration and advanced-packaging competition — is the moatnarrowing at the back end?
The debate: Two linked questions. Arete's Jim Fontanelli flagged top-five customer exposure as "meaningfully largerthan at any point in your history"; BofA's Haas Liu asked whether rising back-end competition, "especially coming from
Intel EMIB-T" [116], cannibalizes the front-to-back-end value capture.Bull view: Management dismissed concentration outright — "No, that's not our concern... the customers are growing
bigger and bigger, we are very happy about it", and argued the customer base is in fact broadening because "there's a
lot of new player in the AI industry" [114]. TSMC is also extending the packaging roadmap beyond 14x-reticle CoWoSinto glass substrates with a pilot line approx. a year from production maturity, and COUPE co-packaged optics has
entered production. On the structural question, Wei's only forward statement was that "next few years is going to be avery good business for TSMC" [116].
Bear view: The deflection is the datapoint. Concentration is rising, TSMC declined to quantify it, and it declined to
quantify the demand-supply gap too [118]. Advanced packaging is being partially outsourced at the margin — TSMCsigned a five-year, $2bn agreement with GlobalFoundries for CoWoS silicon interposers out of Malta, New York,
ramping in 1H28 [59] — which is supply-chain prudence but also evidence that TSMC does not intend to own everystep. And TSMC has consistently refused to break packaging capex out from the 10–20% "packaging, testing, mask
making and others" bucket [110], leaving investors unable to size the back-end business they are being asked to
underwrite.Status into this print: unresolved and under-discussed. This is the debate most likely to be re-litigated if the stock
does not work on a good number. Watch the 3Q26 10-K-equivalent disclosure cadence on customer concentrationand the HPC platform share.

8. Setup & Positioning
Beat/miss history: see §6 — 8/8 versus consensus on both lines, 5/5 versus the revenue guide midpoint where theguide is on file, all under the current Wei/Huang team [3][4][89][91].
Typical T+1 reaction (close on report day → close on the next session, Source: S&P Global):
Print Report date Close on reportday Close T+1 T+1 move
Q3 2025 2025-10-16 NT$1,485 NT$1,450 −2.4%
Q4 2025 2026-01-15 NT$1,690 NT$1,740 +3.0%
Q1 2026 2026-04-16 NT$2,085 NT$2,030 −2.6%
Q2 2026 2026-07-16 NT$2,470 NT$2,290 −7.3%
TSMC has fallen on T+1 after three of its last four prints, averaging approx. −2.3%, despite beating consensus
revenue and EPS in all four [4]. The 2Q26 reaction is the one to internalize: the company beat EPS by 12.6% [4], raised
the FY guide [111], raised capex by $8bn [110] and announced $100bn more for Arizona [78] — and the stock fell 7.3%the next session on 95.8m shares, more than triple the prior day's volume (Source: S&P Global). The pattern repeated on
the September monthly release: an above-guidance quarter, and the ADR closed −3% at $457.99 [107]. The same sell-the-news behaviour hit Samsung and SK hynix on 2026-10-08 [65][70].
Expectations bar into the print: HIGH.
The revenue beat is already public and already traded [107]; it is no longer a surprise asset.The stock is up approximately 60% year to date from NT$1,585 at end-2025 [21] and sits NT$45 (−1.7%) below its
NT$2,585 record close of 2026-10-06/07 (Source: S&P Global). The ADR 52-week range is $266.82–$479.00 withthe high set this month [102].
Sell-side positioning is at an extreme: 39 of 42 analysts at Buy or Overweight, zero below Hold, weighted score 1.13
[62].The capex expectation has been pre-marked to $85bn for 2027 [6] — a number TSMC has never guided to and
explicitly declined to frame in July [112].The §6 calibration read cuts the other way, and is the reason the bar is high-but-not-unclearable: because the current
team has tightened the revenue guide to within approx. 2% while the Street keeps under-modelling EPS by 5–13%, the
earnings bar is genuinely lower than the narrative bar. The quarter's EPS can beat by 5–7% on arithmetic alone (§1)without a single new piece of good news.
Options-implied move: not retrievable from a dated source for 2330-TW or TSM into this print — omitted rather than
estimated. For calibration, the four observed T+1 moves above span −7.3% to +3.0%.
Bottom line
What is priced: a record quarter, a beat, and a bullish AI narrative — all three are already in the stock after a approx. 60%
year-to-date run to within 2% of an all-time high, with 39 of 42 analysts at Buy or better [21][62]. Because TSMC pre-releases monthly revenue, the 3Q26 top line is a published fact — NT$1,494.24bn, approx. $46.7bn, above the high
end of its own guide and 2.1% above consensus [13][17][15][109][1] — and the market has already sold that fact once,
on 2026-10-08 [107]. What would surprise: not revenue, but (a) the 4Q26 margin guide holding 65%+ with N2 at fulldilution and a firmer TWD [109]; (b) an EPS print toward NT$30+, which is what the 56–58% operating-margin guide
mechanically implies on already-disclosed revenue against a NT$28.55 consensus (§1) — the §6 pattern of EPS beats
averaging +8.8% over the last four quarters while revenue beats compressed to under 2% says this is the likelier side of
the distribution; and (c) any quantified 2027 frame — a capex range, a revenue-growth number, or confirmation of thereported 3–6% wafer price increases [53] — all three of which management refused to give in July [112][117][113]. The
swing factor is the 2027 capex number, and it carries sequencing risk: ASML's bookings and 2027 outlook land on2026-10-14, one day before TSMC speaks [63], against a sell-side bar already at $85bn [6]. Net cross-read is Positive
and unusually well corroborated — NVIDIA guiding $108bn and approx. 70% FY28 growth while calling itself supply-
constrained [38][48], Micron at $54.2bn and 87% gross margin with an 8%-above-consensus guide [24][26], Samsungat a KRW107.4tn operating profit [64][67], TSMC's own monthly line accelerating to +54.6% YoY [5], and foundry share
holding at 72.5% [82]. The asymmetry is therefore not about whether the business is good; it is margin-and-2027versus a very high narrative bar. The clean beat is in the earnings line because the Street has mis-modelled it for eight
straight quarters; the risk is that a fourth consecutive sell-the-news T+1 happens anyway, because the only genuinely
unpriced disclosure on this call — a 2027 capex range — is the one management has spent two quarters refusing to give,and the one the stock has already paid for.

Report expected Thursday 2026-10-15, 06:00 UTC (14:00 Taipei) — company-confirmed earnings event | last price

only) | consensus coverage 29 est. revenue / 28 est. EPS for the quarter [1]. TSMC's fiscal year is the calendar year(Dec-31 year-end), so fiscal and calendar labels coincide [1][23].
1. Expectations
The defining feature of this print: the revenue line is already public. TSMC discloses monthly revenue, so 3Q26 top-
line is a reported actual, not an estimate — NT$467.58bn (Jul) + NT$514.81bn (Aug) + NT$511.86bn (Sep) =NT$1,494.24bn [13][17], with the September report filed 2026-10-08 [5][7]. That is above the top of the company's own
USD guide and above consensus. The print therefore hinges on margins, the 4Q26 guide, and the first real framing of2027 capex — not on revenue.

The guidance range and all YoY margin comparisons in this note are stated on the company's own basis unless markedFactSet-computed.
Setup thesis — five points:
Revenue is a done deal and it beat. NT$1,494.24bn is +2.4% above the TWD-equivalent guide midpoint(NT$1,459.0bn [3]) and +2.1% above the NT$1,463.9bn consensus [1]. Reuters' LSEG SmartEstimate from 19
analysts sat at NT$1.46tn [15]; pre-disclosure, the Street looked for approx. $45.44bn and $4.42 per ADR [107]. Thesurprise has already been monetized — the stock fell 3% on the ADR line the day the September number landed [107].
FX was a non-event, which makes the beat a real volume/mix beat. USD/TWD averaged approx. 31.97 across 3Q26
(31.9–32.4 in July, 31.5–32.0 in August, 31.7–31.9 in September; 31.874 on 2026-09-30, 31.93 on 2026-10-12)(Source: FMP), essentially on top of the TWD32 guidance assumption [109]. The upside is therefore wafer output and
mix, not translation.The margin line is where the print is actually decided, and the bar embeds a self-inflicted drag. Management
guided GM down approx. 1.7pp sequentially to 66% at the midpoint because the steep N2 ramp dilutes gross margin
by 3–4 percentage points in 2H26, with overseas-fab dilution running 2–3pp now and widening to 3–4pp in laterstages [109]. N2 was only 3% of wafer revenue in 2Q26 [119], so the ramp — and its dilution — is barely begun.
Consensus EPS sits at the bottom of the band the guide itself implies. Taking the disclosed NT$1,494.24bnrevenue and the 56–58% operating-margin guide [109] gives operating profit of NT$836.8–866.7bn (NT$851.7bn at
the 57% midpoint). Applying the net-income-to-operating-profit conversion observed over the last four reported
quarters (3Q25 90.3%, 4Q25 89.7%, 1Q26 87.1%, 2Q26 92.8% [23]) to the 57% midpoint gives net income ofNT$741.8–790.4bn and, on approx. 25.93bn diluted shares (derived from 2Q26 net income NT$706.56bn ÷ EPS
NT$27.247 [23]), EPS of NT$28.6–30.5. Consensus is NT$28.55 [1] and LSEG's SmartEstimate implies approx.
NT$28.8 [101] — i.e. the Street is pinned to the floor of the guide-implied range. (This bridge is our own calculation; itis sensitive to non-operating income and the tax rate, which moved the conversion ratio by 5.7pp across the last four
quarters.)The one thing that can genuinely surprise is 2027. Management refused a three-year capex number in July [112]
while saying the next three years' capex will be "even more significantly higher than the past three years", and refused
to update the five-year AI CAGR other than to call it "stronger and stronger and stronger" [117]. US sell-side has sincemarked 2027/2028 capex estimates to $85bn / $98bn [6], and Taiwanese media report TSMC has locked in 3–6%
wafer price increases for 2027 across N2/N3 (blended approx. 5%), which TSMC has not confirmed [53][16][52]. Afirst 2027 revenue-growth or capex frame is the highest-variance item on the call.

Raise / reaffirm / cut read on the FY26 guide: RAISE, high confidence. 9M26 revenue of NT$3,898.73bn is +41.1% YoY
[5], and 4Q26 quarterly consensus of NT$1,613.09bn [1] on top of that implies approx. +44.7% FY26 growth in TWD."Slightly above 40%" in USD was set on 2026-07-16 before three consecutive monthly records; with Q3 landing above
the guide's own ceiling, reaffirming "slightly above 40%" would be a deliberate sandbag rather than a forecast. Themechanism is also intact on management's own description: AI demand "extremely robust", cloud customers and
customers' customers giving "very strong signal", and the newly flagged agentic-AI CPU resurgence adding silicon
demand on top of accelerators across x86, ARM and RISC-V — "they are almost all TSMC's customers" [111]. Against
that, management explicitly reserved caution for the consumer and price-sensitive end markets, "challenged due tothe impact of rising component prices and macroeconomics uncertainties", and said it is "being prudent in our business
planning" [111] — the one sentence a bear can hold onto.SBC: not a material line for TSMC and not a non-GAAP bridge item — the company guides and reports on IFRS and
publishes no adjusted-EPS measure, so there is no non-GAAP/GAAP gap to flag. The corollary matters for §6: TSMC
issues no EPS guidance, so "beat vs own guide" can only be measured on revenue and margin.
3. Key Debates from the Last Call
Debate 1: Is the N2 + overseas-fab margin dilution a two-quarter air pocket or a multi-year reset of the margin ceiling?
The debate: TSMC guided gross margin down approx. 1.7pp sequentially even as revenue stepped up 12% — can the
company hold a mid-60s gross margin through the steepest node ramp and the largest overseas build-out in itshistory?
Bull view: The dilution is mechanical and front-loaded. N2 was just 3% of wafer revenue in 2Q26 [119]; yields and
overhead absorption improve every quarter from here, and management named the offsets — "very strong demandfor our leading-edge technologies and continued cost improvement efforts, including productivity gains and across-
node capacity optimization" [109]. Pricing is the other lever: reported 3–6% wafer price increases effective January
2027 would land just as N2 dilution peaks [53][16]. 2Q26 gross margin of 67.7% came in above guidance on costimprovement and utilization [78].
Bear view: The drags stack rather than offset. Management quantified N2 dilution at 3–4pp for all of 2H26 andsimultaneously reiterated overseas dilution of 2–3pp "in the early stages", widening to 3–4pp in the latter stages over
the next several years [109]. With 12 planned US facilities and approx. 30% of leading-edge N2-and-beyond capacity
eventually in Arizona [78], plus a potential Texas campus [86][84], the overseas mix only grows. Add "we have nocontrol over the foreign exchange rate" [109] and the 65-67% guide starts to look like the new normal rather than a
trough.What the last print showed: 2Q26 gross margin 67.7%, operating margin 60.3%, net margin 55.6% on revenue of
$40.20bn / NT$1,270.38bn [78] — a sequential gross-margin gain of 150bp driven by cost work and utilization, partly
offset by overseas-fab dilution [109]. FactSet-computed gross margin has risen from 51.7% in 2Q24 to 66.7% in 2Q26[23], i.e. the structural trend has been up through the entire build-out so far.
Status into this print: leaning bull, but unresolved. Revenue came in 2.4% above the TWD-equivalent guidemidpoint [3][13] with FX at the assumption — operating leverage on unguided volume should push margins toward the
upper half of the range. The genuine unknown is the 4Q26 margin guide, which is the first quarter to carry a full N2
quarter plus incremental Arizona ramp.
Debate 2: How much more capex, and does the capital-intensity step-up break thereturns story?
The debate: Capex has been raised twice in 2026 — $52–56bn in January, "closer to $56bn" in April, $60–64bn now
[110]. Analysts pressed four separate times for a multi-year number and did not get one.
Bull view: Capex is demand-pull, not speculative. Management's framing is explicit: "a higher level of capitalexpenditures is always correlated to higher growth opportunities in the following years" [110], and on the driver of the
raise, "demand continue to increase and we feel the pressure from the customer... for the capacity increase" [115]. Thethree-year capex statement was upgraded mid-sentence from "significantly higher" to "even more significantly higher
than the past three years" [112]. Demand still exceeds supply by what the CEO would only characterize as "a very big
gap" [118]. No bottleneck is foreseen because tool suppliers are engaged years ahead [110].
Bear view: Part of the increase is price, not capacity — "the second reason is inflation. Now, we buy the tools with the
inflation price" [115], and separately TSMC and ASML are reported to be in a cycle of equipment price increases [53].Deputy Co-COO Cliff Hou has said the company has had to roughly double planned equipment purchases over the
past year [84]. If a chunk of the $8bn raise buys the same wafers at a higher price, incremental ROIC degrades,depreciation steps up into 2027–28, and the gross-margin reset in Debate 1 becomes permanent. Management also
declined to break out advanced packaging capex separately despite being asked to — "we cannot very specifically
say which area we put how much of the CapEx" [110].What the last print showed: 2Q26 capex of NT$496bn / US$15.7bn, against NT$783bn of operating cash flow [119]
— the spend is still internally funded with room to spare, and the cash balance rose NT$99bn to NT$3.1tn in thequarter with NT$3.5tn / $110bn of cash and marketable securities [119].
Status into this print: unresolved, and the single highest-variance item. Sell-side is now at $85bn (2027E) and
$98bn (2028E) [6]. Any 2027 capex frame on the call — even a range — immediately re-rates the whole WFEcomplex, and ASML reports the day before [63].
Debate 3: Will TSMC monetize the shortage through price, and how is it being valuedagainst memory?
The debate: Memory peers are earning extraordinary margins off the same AI shortage. Gokul Hariharan asked
directly whether TSMC's foundry role deserves better long-term profitability and what pricing approach it would take.Bull view: TSMC has the pricing power and is beginning to use it. Reports point to 3–6% wafer price increases from
January 2027 on N2/N3, approx. 5% blended, hitting Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm and Apple [53][52][16].Order visibility on mature nodes reportedly extends toward 2030 [52]. TSMC held 72.5% of the foundry market in
2Q26 per TrendForce [82]; no customer has an alternative at N2.
Bear view: Management has pre-committed itself against opportunistic pricing: "we don't suddenly increase our priceby which I like to have, 4x or 5x" — the customer "got to be successful... I don't want to squeeze them out from the
market" [113]. That is a deliberate choice to leave value on the table, and Wei said so almost explicitly in the sameanswer when he compared TSMC's margin to memory's and conceded he would not be happy at 68% [113]. The read-
through: TSMC's margin ceiling is a policy variable set below the economic maximum, which caps the re-rating a
shortage can deliver.What the last print showed: No price action was announced or confirmed; the 3Q26 guide carried no pricing
commentary beyond cost improvement and mix [109]. Mature-node tightness was described as narrow, not broad —only AI-adjacent mature nodes (power management IC at 0.18µm/90nm, sensors) are short, while "the consumer
product is not in a high demand" and other segments are "not so much of, say, in a lot of shortage. Not at all" [115].
Status into this print: leaning bull on realization, leaning bear on magnitude. Expect the question to be asked againon 10-15; expect management to decline to confirm specifics, as it has done for every pricing question to date. Any
confirmation of a 2027 price increase is a clear positive for 2027 consensus margins.
Debate 4: Customer concentration and advanced-packaging competition — is the moatnarrowing at the back end?
The debate: Two linked questions. Arete's Jim Fontanelli flagged top-five customer exposure as "meaningfully largerthan at any point in your history"; BofA's Haas Liu asked whether rising back-end competition, "especially coming from
Intel EMIB-T" [116], cannibalizes the front-to-back-end value capture.Bull view: Management dismissed concentration outright — "No, that's not our concern... the customers are growing
bigger and bigger, we are very happy about it", and argued the customer base is in fact broadening because "there's a
lot of new player in the AI industry" [114]. TSMC is also extending the packaging roadmap beyond 14x-reticle CoWoSinto glass substrates with a pilot line approx. a year from production maturity, and COUPE co-packaged optics has
entered production. On the structural question, Wei's only forward statement was that "next few years is going to be avery good business for TSMC" [116].
Bear view: The deflection is the datapoint. Concentration is rising, TSMC declined to quantify it, and it declined to
quantify the demand-supply gap too [118]. Advanced packaging is being partially outsourced at the margin — TSMCsigned a five-year, $2bn agreement with GlobalFoundries for CoWoS silicon interposers out of Malta, New York,
ramping in 1H28 [59] — which is supply-chain prudence but also evidence that TSMC does not intend to own everystep. And TSMC has consistently refused to break packaging capex out from the 10–20% "packaging, testing, mask
making and others" bucket [110], leaving investors unable to size the back-end business they are being asked to
underwrite.Status into this print: unresolved and under-discussed. This is the debate most likely to be re-litigated if the stock
does not work on a good number. Watch the 3Q26 10-K-equivalent disclosure cadence on customer concentrationand the HPC platform share.

The current-vs-prior-management split: there is no split, and that is the finding. C.C. Wei has been CEO since
June 2018 and Chairman and CEO since 4 June 2024 [89][91][92]; Wendell Huang has been CFO since 2019 anddelivered the guidance on every call in this window, including the 2Q26 call [91][90]. Every one of these eight guides
— issued from the October 2024 call through the July 2026 call — was set by today's team. There is therefore nohandover artefact inflating the streak: the beat record is a clean read on the calibration of the people who will set the
4Q26 guide on 10-15. The flip side is that there is also no "prior-regime sandbagger" excuse available to discount the
streak.The trend inside the current team's record is the actionable part — revenue guidance has become more precise
while EPS consensus has become less accurate. Revenue-versus-guide beats peaked at +4.2% in Q4 2025 andhave compressed to +2.1% and +1.8% in the last two quarters [3][4] — the revenue guide is tightening toward reality.

+8.8% (+9.7%, +7.2%, +5.5%, +12.6%) against approx. +4.6% for the four before them (+9.1%, +0.8%, +2.4%, +6.1%)[4]. The gap is not revenue; it is that the Street persistently under-models the margin and non-operating lines relative

number: consensus of NT$28.55 sits at the bottom of the NT$28.6–30.5 band the 56–58% operating-margin guideimplies on already-disclosed revenue.

year-to-date run to within 2% of an all-time high, with 39 of 42 analysts at Buy or better [21][62]. Because TSMC pre-releases monthly revenue, the 3Q26 top line is a published fact — NT$1,494.24bn, approx. $46.7bn, above the high
end of its own guide and 2.1% above consensus [13][17][15][109][1] — and the market has already sold that fact once,
on 2026-10-08 [107]. What would surprise: not revenue, but (a) the 4Q26 margin guide holding 65%+ with N2 at fulldilution and a firmer TWD [109]; (b) an EPS print toward NT$30+, which is what the 56–58% operating-margin guide
mechanically implies on already-disclosed revenue against a NT$28.55 consensus (§1) — the §6 pattern of EPS beats
averaging +8.8% over the last four quarters while revenue beats compressed to under 2% says this is the likelier side of
the distribution; and (c) any quantified 2027 frame — a capex range, a revenue-growth number, or confirmation of thereported 3–6% wafer price increases [53] — all three of which management refused to give in July [112][117][113]. The
swing factor is the 2027 capex number, and it carries sequencing risk: ASML's bookings and 2027 outlook land on2026-10-14, one day before TSMC speaks [63], against a sell-side bar already at $85bn [6]. Net cross-read is Positive
and unusually well corroborated — NVIDIA guiding $108bn and approx. 70% FY28 growth while calling itself supply-
constrained [38][48], Micron at $54.2bn and 87% gross margin with an 8%-above-consensus guide [24][26], Samsungat a KRW107.4tn operating profit [64][67], TSMC's own monthly line accelerating to +54.6% YoY [5], and foundry share
holding at 72.5% [82]. The asymmetry is therefore not about whether the business is good; it is margin-and-2027versus a very high narrative bar. The clean beat is in the earnings line because the Street has mis-modelled it for eight
straight quarters; the risk is that a fourth consecutive sell-the-news T+1 happens anyway, because the only genuinely
unpriced disclosure on this call — a 2027 capex range — is the one management has spent two quarters refusing to give,and the one the stock has already paid for.

⭐️即時資訊_獲利公告—中信金(2891 TT )

2026/10/14

💎訊息內容

中信金(2891 TT)公告前9月調整後獲利年增116%至1,315億元，優於預期。

💎評論及分析

1. 中信金9月稅後淨利93.6億元，月減6%、年減16%，加計金控FVOCI股票資本利得176億元之調整後獲利269.6億元，月增3.6%，其中中信銀獲利月增0.3%(淨利差上揚提升淨利息收入、呆帳提存僅0.2億元，抵銷手收及投資收益減少)，加上創投認列獲利14億元反映投資部位評價回升，抵銷台壽保獲利月減58%至12.9億元。

2. 中信金3Q26稅後淨利237億元，季增44%、年減5%，若加上7-9月穩定實現FVOCI股票資本利得合計265億元，3Q26調整後獲利775億元，季增81%、年增211%。中信金前9月獲利年增4%至633億元(每股盈餘3.18元)，調整後獲利年增116%至1,315億元(每股盈餘6.68元)，達凱基全年預估76%及104%，優於預期。

3. 凱基前一次對中信金研究報告為「增加持股」評等，目標價74元 (基於總和評量法模型，約2026F-27F股價淨值比1.9倍)，主要看好中信銀2026F淨利息收入年增超過雙位數反映外幣放款受惠供應鏈移轉，資本市場熱絡帶動手續費收入達雙位數成長，加上台壽保FVOCI股票資本利得挹注中信金調整後獲利年增57%以上，提升每股現金股利至2.8-3元。

【僅供內部參考，請勿外傳】

🔥凱基投顧 劉昃恩 (Jenny)

 ⭐️KGI Radar Monthly—消費產業: 消費放緩風險揮之不去

 2026/10/14

 💎結論建議

由於以出口導向為主消費族群可能持續面臨需求放緩及價格壓力，我們建議關注 3Q26 財報可望優於預期、且 2027 年獲利成長展望穩健之利基型類股。凱基偏好個股包括：華航 (2610 TT， NT$20.65，增加持股)、長榮航 (2618 TT，NT$43.4，增加持股) 、望隼 (4771 TT， NT$205.5，增加持股)、視陽 (6782 TT，NT$244.5，增加持股)、巨大 (9921 TT，NT$92.1，增加持股)、美利達 (9914 TT， NT$66.7 ，增加持股) 、八方雲集 (2753 TT， NT$184 ，增加持股) 、王品 (2727 TT，NT$242，增加持股)。

💎重點摘要 

1. 美國消費指標走低，放大投資者對購物旺季之擔憂。儘管今年迄今美國零售銷售展現超乎預期的韌性，全球運動休閒品牌及零售商2Q26財報顯示2H26庫存去化已成定局，且近期更多指標浮現消費降溫早期跡象。8月信用卡及其他循環信貸餘額減少48億美元，創下2024年11月以來最大單月減幅；這透露在居高不下的油價與高利率壓力時間拉長下，民眾已從「因漲價預期而提前囤貨」轉向「償還部分卡債」，信用擴張所創造的額外購買力步入收縮。10月密大消費者信心指數進一步惡化至46.3，連續三個月下滑，並逼近歷史低點，反映投資人對即將而來的購物旺季消費力道充滿疑慮。

2. 9月營收回顧。在台灣消費次產業中，貨櫃、散裝及航空業為9月營收成長最快之族群，分別年增73%、29%、35%，遠優於過去十年同期平均水準。貨櫃航運主要受美國政府退稅刺激庫存回補帶動，散裝航運得益於美洲穀物及鐵礦砂旺季出口強勁。AI相關貨運的高需求挹注航空業成長延續。在外銷族群中，成衣及製鞋業9月營收分別改善至年增11%、9%，係因低基期與匯率正面貢獻。受新舊車款過渡期影響，自行車品牌廠9月營收年減4%。

3. 3Q26財報預覽。我們初步分析3Q26財報可望優於預期族群包括貨櫃航運、航空及隱形眼鏡。貨櫃航商中萬海 (2615 TT，NT$125，增加持股) 表現應最為突出，主因佔其貨量比重超過50%之近洋線運價漲幅超前。航空業將受惠暑假旅遊旺季及AI產品空運出口之雙重加持。隱形眼鏡則因產品組合有利及產能利用率滿載，3Q26利潤率及獲利潛在上檔。整體而言，3Q26台幣貶值對出口導向消費產業將有業外加分。內需方面，台灣2H26假期較多將有助於餐飲業者營收與獲利佳績延伸。

【僅供內部參考，請勿外傳】

9 月營收回顧。 在台灣消費次產業中，貨櫃、散裝及航空業為 9 月營收成長
最快之族群，分別年增 73%、29%、35%，遠優於過去十年同期平均水準。
貨櫃航運主要受美國政府退稅刺激庫存回補帶動，散裝航運得益於美洲穀物
及鐵礦砂旺季出口強勁。A I 相關貨運的高需求挹注航空業成長延續。在外銷
族群中，成衣及製鞋業 9 月營收分別改善至年增 11%、9%，係因低基期與
匯率正面貢獻。受新舊車款過渡期影響，自行車品牌廠 9 月營收年減 4%。 
3Q26 財報預覽 。我們初 步分析 3Q26 財報可望優於預期族群包括貨櫃航運、
航空及隱形眼鏡。貨櫃航商中萬海 (2615 TT，NT$125，增加持股) 表現應最
為突出，主因佔其貨量 比重超過 50%之近洋線運價漲幅超前。航空業將受惠
暑假旅遊旺季及 AI 產品空運出口之雙重加持。隱形眼鏡則因產品組合有利及
產能利用率滿載， 3Q26 利潤率及獲利潛在上檔。整體而言， 3Q26 台幣貶值
對出口導向消費產業將有業外加分。內需方面，台灣 2H26 假期較多將有助
於餐飲業者營收與獲利佳績延伸。  
投資建議  
由於以出口導向為主消費族群可能持續面臨需求放緩及價格壓力，我們建議
關注 3Q26 財報可望優於預期 、 且2027 年獲利成長展望穩健之利基型類股。

零售 
 
圖 44：零售產業摘要  圖 45：8 月台灣零售銷售成長放緩 
1. 台灣 8 月零售銷售年增 6.5%，維持穩健成長動能，主要受惠中
元普渡及中秋禮盒採買需求、百貨新商場與新品牌加入。其中超
級市場表現最佳，年增 8.7%，百貨公司及便利商店則分別年增 
8.4% 與 2.9%。 
2. 台灣 8 月餐飲業營業年增 1.8%，增幅較上月收斂，主要受農曆
七月影響餐廳婚宴收入，加上降雨天數增加影響來客數，抵銷暑
假假期聚餐需求。 
3. 中國消費動能持續放緩， 8 月餐飲收入年增率由 1.4%降至
1.1%，零售銷售年增率亦由 0.6%收斂至 0.4%。

 ⭐️KGI Radar Monthly—消費產業: 消費放緩風險揮之不去

 2026/10/14

 💎結論建議

考量美伊衝突再起恐將干擾台灣外銷消費產業營收回升之延續性，我們建議保持防禦型操作。凱基偏好獲利潛在上檔之利基型消費類股標的，包括：長榮航 (2618 TT，NT$40.8，增加持股)、巨大 (9921 TT，NT$81.3，增加持股)、美利達 (9914 TT，NT$76.1，增加持股)、望隼 (4771 TT，NT$205，增加持股)、視陽 (6782 TT，NT$198.5，增加持股)。

💎重點摘要 

1. 美國消費指標走低，放大投資者對購物旺季之擔憂。儘管今年迄今美國零售銷售展現超乎預期的韌性，全球運動休閒品牌及零售商2Q26財報顯示2H26庫存去化已成定局，且近期更多指標浮現消費降溫早期跡象。8月信用卡及其他循環信貸餘額減少48億美元，創下2024年11月以來最大單月減幅；這透露在居高不下的油價與高利率壓力時間拉長下，民眾已從「因漲價預期而提前囤貨」轉向「償還部分卡債」，信用擴張所創造的額外購買力步入收縮。10月密大消費者信心指數進一步惡化至46.3，連續三個月下滑，並逼近歷史低點，反映投資人對即將而來的購物旺季消費力道充滿疑慮。

2. 9月營收回顧。在台灣消費次產業中，貨櫃、散裝及航空業為9月營收成長最快之族群，分別年增73%、29%、35%，遠優於過去十年同期平均水準。貨櫃航運主要受美國政府退稅刺激庫存回補帶動，散裝航運得益於美洲穀物及鐵礦砂旺季出口強勁。AI相關貨運的高需求挹注航空業成長延續。在外銷族群中，成衣及製鞋業9月營收分別改善至年增11%、9%，係因低基期與匯率正面貢獻。受新舊車款過渡期影響，自行車品牌廠9月營收年減4%。

3. 3Q26財報預覽。我們初步分析3Q26財報可望優於預期族群包括貨櫃航運、航空及隱形眼鏡。貨櫃航商中萬海 (2615 TT，NT$125，增加持股) 表現應最為突出，主因佔其貨量比重超過50%之近洋線運價漲幅超前。航空業將受惠暑假旅遊旺季及AI產品空運出口之雙重加持。隱形眼鏡則因產品組合有利及產能利用率滿載，3Q26利潤率及獲利潛在上檔。整體而言，3Q26台幣貶值對出口導向消費產業將有業外加分。內需方面，台灣2H26假期較多將有助於餐飲業者營收與獲利佳績延伸。

Nike (美) 公布 1Q FY27 (6 -8 月 ； 財年止於5 月) 營收年減 4%至 112 億美元，
低於市場預估，主因 Nike 運動休閒系列、 Jordan 品牌及大中華區表現疲軟。
考量消費者購買謹慎與客流量不足 ， 管理層預計 FY27 營收將年減高個位數，
隱含 2Q-4Q FY27 營收衰退擴大。因此，公司計畫進一步清理過剩庫存 。繼
Air Jordan 1 (AJ1 ) 及 Dunk 供應減量後，未來 Jordan 特定復古鞋款發售頻率
也將降低，力求恢復供應稀缺模式；這對於豐泰 (9910 TT ，持有，NT$67.5)
訂單展望將造成負面影響。

假假期聚餐需求。

🔥凱基投顧 劉昃恩 (Jenny)

 ⭐️KGI Radar Monthly—消費產業: 消費放緩風險揮之不去

 2026/10/14

 💎結論建議

考量美伊衝突再起恐將干擾台灣外銷消費產業營收回升之延續性，我們建議保持防禦型操作。凱基偏好獲利潛在上檔之利基型消費類股標的，包括：長榮航 (2618 TT，NT$40.8，增加持股)、巨大 (9921 TT，NT$81.3，增加持股)、美利達 (9914 TT，NT$76.1，增加持股)、望隼 (4771 TT，NT$205，增加持股)、視陽 (6782 TT，NT$198.5，增加持股)。

💎重點摘要

1. 美國消費指標走低，放大投資者對購物旺季之擔憂。儘管今年迄今美國零售銷售展現超乎預期的韌性，全球運動休閒品牌及零售商2Q26財報顯示2H26庫存去化已成定局，且近期更多指標浮現消費降溫早期跡象。8月信用卡及其他循環信貸餘額減少48億美元，創下2024年11月以來最大單月減幅；這透露在居高不下的油價與高利率壓力時間拉長下，民眾已從「因漲價預期而提前囤貨」轉向「償還部分卡債」，信用擴張所創造的額外購買力步入收縮。10月密大消費者信心指數進一步惡化至46.3，連續三個月下滑，並逼近歷史低點，反映投資人對即將而來的購物旺季消費力道充滿疑慮。

2. 9月營收回顧。在台灣消費次產業中，貨櫃、散裝及航空業為9月營收成長最快之族群，分別年增73%、29%、35%，遠優於過去十年同期平均水準。貨櫃航運主要受美國政府退稅刺激庫存回補帶動，散裝航運得益於美洲穀物及鐵礦砂旺季出口強勁。AI相關貨運的高需求挹注航空業成長延續。在外銷族群中，成衣及製鞋業9月營收分別改善至年增11%、9%，係因低基期與匯率正面貢獻。受新舊車款過渡期影響，自行車品牌廠9月營收年減4%。

3. 3Q26財報預覽。我們初步分析3Q26財報可望優於預期族群包括貨櫃航運、航空及隱形眼鏡。貨櫃航商中萬海 (2615 TT，NT$125，增加持股) 表現應最為突出，主因佔其貨量比重超過50%之近洋線運價漲幅超前。航空業將受惠暑假旅遊旺季及AI產品空運出口之雙重加持。隱形眼鏡則因產品組合有利及產能利用率滿載，3Q26利潤率及獲利潛在上檔。整體而言，3Q26台幣貶值對出口導向消費產業將有業外加分。內需方面，台灣2H26假期較多將有助於餐飲業者營收與獲利佳績延伸。

Global Markets Research

Disparities between results at Giant and Merida, 
but steady progress with inventory corrections
Sales up 3% y-y at Giant, down 26% at Merida
September sales: Up 3% y-y at Giant, down 26% at Merida
Giant Manufacturing [9921 TT] released September sales data on 8 October, reporting 
sales up 3% y-y and 4% m-m, while Merida Industry [9914 TT] released September sales 
data on 12 October, reporting sales down 26% y-y and 14% m-m. There was thus a clear 
split between the two companies in the relative strength of their September sales 
performance.  
Sales for Giant Manufacturing’s own-brand products were up 26% y-y in September, 
driven by strong sales of mountain bikes and e-bikes in China. Sales in Europe were flat 
y-y. However, sales in Giant Manufacturing’s OEM business fell slightly y-y in September, 
mainly because of the Withhold Release Order issued by US Customs and Border 
Protection and lower orders from customers. Merida explained that it has adopted a 
cautious approach to both orders and shipments this year to accelerate inventory 
reductions at distributors and across distribution channels, and that this has resulted in 
lower sales in January through September.  At the same time, the company is cautiously 
optimistic about the outlook for the bicycle industry next year and plans to introduce 
several new models.
Mixed results at Giant and Merida, but signs of recovery among related companies
Although results were mixed at Taiwan’s two leading bicycle manufacturers, earnings 
among related companies generally improved. September sales at OEM manufacturer 
Ideal Bike increased 56% y-y, while sales at major bicycle-chain producer KMC rose 25%. 
Moreover, looking at Japan's exports of bicycles and parts (Figure 2), exports to China 
turned upward y-y and those to Europe have held flat, which suggests that demand 
remains relatively stable despite consumers holding back on purchases of high-end 
components from Shimano [7309] (Buy). In view of the above, we maintain our view that 
inventory adjustments in the global bicycle industry are nearing their final stage.

Definition of Nomura Group's equity research rating system and sectors
The rating system is a relative system, indicating expected performance against a specific benchmark identified for each individual stock, 
subject to limited management discretion. An analyst’s target price is an assessment of the current intrinsic fair value of the stock based on an 
appropriate valuation methodology determined by the analyst. Valuation methodologies include, but are not limited to, discounted cash flow 
analysis, expected return on equity and multiple analysis. Analysts may also indicate expected absolute upside/downside relative to the stated 
target price, defined as (target price - current price)/current price.
 
STOCKS
A rating of 'Buy', indicates that the analyst expects the stock to outperform the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Neutral', 
indicates that the analyst expects the stock to perform in line with the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Reduce', indicates that 
the analyst expects the stock to underperform the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Suspended', indicates that the rating, target

Target Price

by other risks related to the company or the market, and may not occur if the company's earnings differ from estimates.

September sales
Global Markets Research
13 October 2026
Disparities between results at Giant and Merida,
but steady progress with inventory corrections
Sales up 3% y-y at Giant, down 26% at Merida
September sales: Up 3% y-y at Giant, down 26% at Merida
Giant Manufacturing [9921 TT] released September sales data on 8 October, reporting
sales up 3% y-y and 4% m-m, while Merida Industry [9914 TT] released September sales
data on 12 October, reporting sales down 26% y-y and 14% m-m. There was thus a clear
split between the two companies in the relative strength of their September sales
performance.
Sales for Giant Manufacturing’s own-brand products were up 26% y-y in September,
driven by strong sales of mountain bikes and e-bikes in China. Sales in Europe were flat
y-y. However, sales in Giant Manufacturing’s OEM business fell slightly y-y in September,
mainly because of the Withhold Release Order issued by US Customs and Border
Protection and lower orders from customers. Merida explained that it has adopted a
cautious approach to both orders and shipments this year to accelerate inventory
reductions at distributors and across distribution channels, and that this has resulted in
lower sales in January through September.  At the same time, the company is cautiously
optimistic about the outlook for the bicycle industry next year and plans to introduce
several new models.
Mixed results at Giant and Merida, but signs of recovery among related companies
Although results were mixed at Taiwan’s two leading bicycle manufacturers, earnings
among related companies generally improved. September sales at OEM manufacturer
Ideal Bike increased 56% y-y, while sales at major bicycle-chain producer KMC rose 25%.
Moreover, looking at Japan's exports of bicycles and parts (Figure 2), exports to China
turned upward y-y and those to Europe have held flat, which suggests that demand
remains relatively stable despite consumers holding back on purchases of high-end
components from Shimano [7309] (Buy). In view of the above, we maintain our view that
inventory adjustments in the global bicycle industry are nearing their final stage.

Gogolook三大事業體
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整
⚫ Gogolook 是全球領先的信任科技 (TrustTech) 公司，運用自有防詐資料庫與 AI 技
術，提供消費者防詐、企業端防詐與金融科技服務。Gogolook 擁有全球最齊全的
通訊與數位防詐數據資料庫，涵蓋電話號碼、網址、和虛擬貨幣錢包地址等。

6
whoscall
⚫ whoscall 為 Gogolook 所
開發出的個人數位防詐
APP，全球下載量已突破
1億次，月活躍用戶超過
1,800萬，主要服務市場
涵蓋台灣、泰國、日本、
韓國、香港、巴西、馬
來西亞、菲律賓等。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

7
whoscall海外市場持續擴張
⚫ whoscall海外市場擴張成效卓越，海外營收占比於2025年已突破63%。泰國為
Gogolook最大的海外市場，其用戶規模、營收貢獻已超越台灣，但仍具備很大的
成長空間；公司於曼谷擁有龐大用戶基礎，目前正進軍泰國二、三線城市。菲律
賓與馬來西亞等地已具備百萬等級的活躍用戶，後續成長可期。
⚫ Gogolook於09/2026已正式和泰國政府退休基金(Government Pension Fund，GPF)簽
署MOU，並與國家跨行交易管理與交換公司(National ITMX)及泰國存款保障機構
(Deposit Protection Agency，DPA)合作，將whoscall防詐服務導入GPF體系，涵蓋
退休人員及現職公務員(超過120萬名會員)。此合作有助於同步推廣泰國當地B2C、
B2B業務。
⚫ 為了有效控制獲客成本，Gogolook在海外減少依賴成效較低的數位廣告，轉而與
當地政府、銀行及電信商合作。此外，考量到東南亞信用卡普及率較低，
Gogolook在泰國率先推出的「電信帳單扣款」訂閱模式大獲成功，目前此模式也
與台灣遠傳電信合作，藉此攻佔中高年齡層客群。
8
whoscall海外市場持續擴張
⚫ 針對品牌偏好較強或市場規模較小的國家(如日本與新加坡)，則透過白牌授權策略，
協助當地業者開發自有防詐App並從中分潤。
⚫ whoscall於02/2026~05/2026與日本Rakuten Mobile進行合作，推出「騷擾電話・簡
訊防護」活動，提供申請用戶免費試用，目前開始有試用用戶轉為付費訂閱，有
望挹注2H26日本市場消費者防詐業務成長動能。
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

9
whoscall海外市場持續擴張

品牌雙軸並進。

目前進軍二、三線

10
Gogolook收購ScamAdviser
⚫ 企業端防詐方面，由於各國法規有加重企業防詐責任的趨勢，Gogolook將此業務
視為長期成長動能潛力來源。Gogolook於2024年收購具備超過6,000萬筆網域資料
庫的ScamAdviser後，成功拓展歐美市場。儘管2025年因主動調整部分低毛利率業
務，導致ScamAdviser營收下滑，但其實質獲利反而增加。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整
⚫ ScamAdviser成立於荷蘭阿姆斯
特丹，為全球防詐聯盟GASA
基石成員。ScamAdviser以AI演
算法與資料庫為基礎，開發自
有的網站風險評級技術，與 
Gogolook的企業防詐解決方案
與電話號碼資料庫整合，為全
球最完整的通訊與數位防詐數
據資料庫。
11
Gogolook企業端防詐服務
⚫ 企業端服務主要分為「資料庫授權」與「商譽保護」兩大主軸：(1) 防詐情資方案，
為一種資料庫授權模式，將whoscall的「電話/簡訊」資料庫以及ScamAdviser的
「網域」資料庫，透過API、SDK方式授權給企業。(2) 商譽保護服務，企業的外
部防詐監控中心，協助企業或政府主動在網路上巡邏，偵測並下架冒用其品牌的
假投資廣告、假粉專或釣魚網站。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

12
Agent looker
⚫ 因應Agentic AI時代來臨，Gogolook於09/2026推出新產品Agent looker，工作原理
是在AI agent實際造訪或讀取網頁前，即時進行風險檢測並攔截惡意請求，可有效
避免AI agent被詐騙的風險。
⚫ 核心防護機制與功能：(1)毫秒級即時掃描，當AI Agent讀取外部網頁或執行URL
請求時，Agent Looker會在毫秒內對網頁封包與內容進行深度檢查，攔截惡意腳本、
釣魚網站以及針對 AI 模型的提示詞注入(Prompt Injection)攻擊。(2)Gogolook威脅
情資資料庫驅動。系統底層串接 Gogolook 累積多年的全球防詐騙、釣魚網站與風
險網域黑名單。基於海量真實風險樣本的數據庫，使其能快速且精準地辨識異常
行為。(3)活動稽核日誌。提供視覺化的管理儀表板，完整記錄AI Agent的所有外
部網路互動軌跡，包含造訪過的網址、讀取的網頁片段及最終的安全判定結果，
確保AI運作透明且可追溯。
⚫ Agent looker目前處於封閉測試(Private Beta)階段。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整
13
金融科技-袋鼠金融
⚫ 金融科技為Gogolook於疫情期間因應線上詐騙激增而開創的新業務，包含全台灣
流量最大的金融媒合平台「袋鼠金融Roo.Cash」，以及專攻小額借款的「JUJI招財
麻吉」。袋鼠金融 Roo.Cash與國內金融機構合作，提供200件以上的金融商品方案
智慧比較與媒合。智能問答服務「Roo AI」，可協助用戶在信用卡、貸款、保險、
投資理財與民生優惠資訊中，快速找到最適合的選項。若順利成交，Gogolook即
可藉此獲得媒合收入。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

14
金融科技-JUJI招財麻吉
⚫ JUJI招財麻吉鎖定10萬元以下、傳統銀行不願承作的利基市場，自行舉辦機車貸
款、手機貸款等業務。該業務最核心的優勢在於將whoscall的通話行為數據轉化為
AI風控模型，不僅可嚴格控制核貸率，更將90天延滯率壓在極低水準。目前JUJI
招財麻吉應收分期款餘額持續增加，公司同時也把純風控模型顧問服務輸出至海
外市場，進一步擴大變現能力，2Q26已成功在泰國市場簽訂首批企業訂單。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

15
Gogolook營運策略
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

16
Gogolook營收續增，毛利率維持高檔
⚫ 隨著消費者防詐、企業端防詐、金融科技三大事業皆穩定增長，預估營收呈現穩
定增長趨勢。觀察重點：whoscall於各國推展進度、企業對於agent looker接受度、
招財麻吉貸放額度及壞帳率變化、AI風控模型專案。
⚫ 毛利率有望穩定落於88~90%。
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

17
Gogolook營業費用控管得宜
⚫ 低成本合作取量：減少高成本數位廣告，擴大與政府單位、電信商、銀行合作，
低成本觸及海外客戶。
⚫ AI優化營運效率：利用AI提升工程與內部效率，人力控管但產出持續提升。
⚫ 費用率逐步下滑：隨著營收規模提升，費用控管得宜，2024年營業費用率96.78%，
2025年營業費用率82.29%，預估2026年營業費用率69.21%。
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

18
營運突破關鍵規模，獲利顯著增長
資料來源：群益投顧彙整
⚫ 由於毛利率接近90%，營業費用控管得宜，隨著營收於4Q25突破關鍵規模點後，
獲利表現開始明顯跳升。由於2026年獲利表現優於預期，過往累積虧損大致抵減
完畢，2027年稅率將回升至常態水準，但可有望開始發放現金股利。

Gogolook三大事業體
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整
⚫ Gogolook 是全球領先的信任科技 (TrustTech) 公司，運用自有防詐資料庫與 AI 技
術，提供消費者防詐、企業端防詐與金融科技服務。Gogolook 擁有全球最齊全的
通訊與數位防詐數據資料庫，涵蓋電話號碼、網址、和虛擬貨幣錢包地址等。

whoscall
⚫ whoscall 為 Gogolook 所
開發出的個人數位防詐
APP，全球下載量已突破

資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

whoscall海外市場持續擴張
⚫ whoscall海外市場擴張成效卓越，海外營收占比於2025年已突破63%。泰國為
Gogolook最大的海外市場，其用戶規模、營收貢獻已超越台灣，但仍具備很大的
成長空間；公司於曼谷擁有龐大用戶基礎，目前正進軍泰國二、三線城市。菲律
賓與馬來西亞等地已具備百萬等級的活躍用戶，後續成長可期。
⚫ Gogolook於09/2026已正式和泰國政府退休基金(Government Pension Fund，GPF)簽
署MOU，並與國家跨行交易管理與交換公司(National ITMX)及泰國存款保障機構
(Deposit Protection Agency，DPA)合作，將whoscall防詐服務導入GPF體系，涵蓋
退休人員及現職公務員(超過120萬名會員)。此合作有助於同步推廣泰國當地B2C、
B2B業務。
⚫ 為了有效控制獲客成本，Gogolook在海外減少依賴成效較低的數位廣告，轉而與
當地政府、銀行及電信商合作。此外，考量到東南亞信用卡普及率較低，
Gogolook在泰國率先推出的「電信帳單扣款」訂閱模式大獲成功，目前此模式也
與台灣遠傳電信合作，藉此攻佔中高年齡層客群。

whoscall海外市場持續擴張
⚫ 針對品牌偏好較強或市場規模較小的國家(如日本與新加坡)，則透過白牌授權策略，
協助當地業者開發自有防詐App並從中分潤。
⚫ whoscall於02/2026~05/2026與日本Rakuten Mobile進行合作，推出「騷擾電話・簡
訊防護」活動，提供申請用戶免費試用，目前開始有試用用戶轉為付費訂閱，有
望挹注2H26日本市場消費者防詐業務成長動能。
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

點發展國家。

Gogolook收購ScamAdviser
⚫ 企業端防詐方面，由於各國法規有加重企業防詐責任的趨勢，Gogolook將此業務
視為長期成長動能潛力來源。Gogolook於2024年收購具備超過6,000萬筆網域資料
庫的ScamAdviser後，成功拓展歐美市場。儘管2025年因主動調整部分低毛利率業
務，導致ScamAdviser營收下滑，但其實質獲利反而增加。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整
⚫ ScamAdviser成立於荷蘭阿姆斯
特丹，為全球防詐聯盟GASA
基石成員。ScamAdviser以AI演
算法與資料庫為基礎，開發自
有的網站風險評級技術，與
Gogolook的企業防詐解決方案
與電話號碼資料庫整合，為全
球最完整的通訊與數位防詐數
據資料庫。

Gogolook企業端防詐服務
⚫ 企業端服務主要分為「資料庫授權」與「商譽保護」兩大主軸：(1) 防詐情資方案，
為一種資料庫授權模式，將whoscall的「電話/簡訊」資料庫以及ScamAdviser的
「網域」資料庫，透過API、SDK方式授權給企業。(2) 商譽保護服務，企業的外
部防詐監控中心，協助企業或政府主動在網路上巡邏，偵測並下架冒用其品牌的
假投資廣告、假粉專或釣魚網站。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

Agent looker
⚫ 因應Agentic AI時代來臨，Gogolook於09/2026推出新產品Agent looker，工作原理
是在AI agent實際造訪或讀取網頁前，即時進行風險檢測並攔截惡意請求，可有效
避免AI agent被詐騙的風險。
⚫ 核心防護機制與功能：(1)毫秒級即時掃描，當AI Agent讀取外部網頁或執行URL
請求時，Agent Looker會在毫秒內對網頁封包與內容進行深度檢查，攔截惡意腳本、
釣魚網站以及針對 AI 模型的提示詞注入(Prompt Injection)攻擊。(2)Gogolook威脅
情資資料庫驅動。系統底層串接 Gogolook 累積多年的全球防詐騙、釣魚網站與風
險網域黑名單。基於海量真實風險樣本的數據庫，使其能快速且精準地辨識異常
行為。(3)活動稽核日誌。提供視覺化的管理儀表板，完整記錄AI Agent的所有外
部網路互動軌跡，包含造訪過的網址、讀取的網頁片段及最終的安全判定結果，
確保AI運作透明且可追溯。
⚫ Agent looker目前處於封閉測試(Private Beta)階段。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

金融科技-袋鼠金融
⚫ 金融科技為Gogolook於疫情期間因應線上詐騙激增而開創的新業務，包含全台灣
流量最大的金融媒合平台「袋鼠金融Roo.Cash」，以及專攻小額借款的「JUJI招財
麻吉」。袋鼠金融 Roo.Cash與國內金融機構合作，提供200件以上的金融商品方案
智慧比較與媒合。智能問答服務「Roo AI」，可協助用戶在信用卡、貸款、保險、
投資理財與民生優惠資訊中，快速找到最適合的選項。若順利成交，Gogolook即
可藉此獲得媒合收入。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

金融科技-JUJI招財麻吉
⚫ JUJI招財麻吉鎖定10萬元以下、傳統銀行不願承作的利基市場，自行舉辦機車貸
款、手機貸款等業務。該業務最核心的優勢在於將whoscall的通話行為數據轉化為
AI風控模型，不僅可嚴格控制核貸率，更將90天延滯率壓在極低水準。目前JUJI
招財麻吉應收分期款餘額持續增加，公司同時也把純風控模型顧問服務輸出至海
外市場，進一步擴大變現能力，2Q26已成功在泰國市場簽訂首批企業訂單。
資料來源：Gogolook、群益投顧彙整

Gogolook營運策略
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

Gogolook營收續增，毛利率維持高檔
⚫ 隨著消費者防詐、企業端防詐、金融科技三大事業皆穩定增長，預估營收呈現穩
定增長趨勢。觀察重點：whoscall於各國推展進度、企業對於agent looker接受度、
招財麻吉貸放額度及壞帳率變化、AI風控模型專案。
⚫ 毛利率有望穩定落於88~90%。
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

Gogolook營業費用控管得宜
⚫ 低成本合作取量：減少高成本數位廣告，擴大與政府單位、電信商、銀行合作，
低成本觸及海外客戶。
⚫ AI優化營運效率：利用AI提升工程與內部效率，人力控管但產出持續提升。
⚫ 費用率逐步下滑：隨著營收規模提升，費用控管得宜，2024年營業費用率96.78%，
2025年營業費用率82.29%，預估2026年營業費用率69.21%。
資料來源：群益投顧彙整

營運突破關鍵規模，獲利顯著增長
資料來源：群益投顧彙整
⚫ 由於毛利率接近90%，營業費用控管得宜，隨著營收於4Q25突破關鍵規模點後，
獲利表現開始明顯跳升。由於2026年獲利表現優於預期，過往累積虧損大致抵減
完畢，2027年稅率將回升至常態水準，但可有望開始發放現金股利。

萊德光電-KY(7717.TT) 
產業：電子–通信網路 
衛星網狀網路需求增加，雷射通訊產品出貨倍增 
 投資評價與建議 
受惠低軌衛星雷射通訊產品需求增加，預估 2026/2027 年 稅 後 EPS 為
10.06/13.48元，參考低軌衛星同業產業上行期Forward PE區間多落在30~50
倍，考量低軌衛星進入高速部署期，有利評價上修，給予50倍PER。 
 重點評論分析 
接獲美中光通訊被動與光纖雷射訂單，2Q26營收增加，3Q26營收持續走升：
2Q26營收季增30.2%至3.3億元，係因低軌衛星雷射通訊產品需求增加，另外
接獲傳統光通訊被動元件與高功率光纖雷射訂單，2Q26毛利率受惠產品組合
優化季增6.42ppts，稅後EPS為2.77元。隨低軌衛星進入高速部署期帶動雷射
通訊產品出貨量增加 ， 3Q26營收季增1.4%至3.4億元 ， 預估稅後EPS為2.65元 。  
低軌衛星即將商業運轉，近年迎獲利爆發期：低軌衛星透過底部的雷射光通訊
終端設備(LCT)進行衛星間資料傳輸，單顆衛星約需採用3~4個LCT模組，每顆
LCT均需光放大器，萊德光電主要提供光放大器內部之合束器、隔離器及雷射
輸出端接頭，而兩大美系低軌衛星營運商皆為其客戶。由於目前衛星通訊頻寬
仍受限且尚無法手機直連，故近期發展趨勢為增加單顆衛星上的LCT雷射通訊
終端數量，未來若太空資料中心計畫被採用，LCT模組用量可望提升至6顆，用
量倍增，另外同步提高單顆LCT頻寬與功率，由於太空對於封裝與散熱規格的
要求將更加嚴苛，產品單價與技術門檻亦大幅提升。 
 投資風險

功率光纖雷射產品訂單，1Q26毛利率僅57.5%，受備抵存貨影響，2Q26毛利率則受惠衛星產品出貨增加帶動產
品組合優化季增6.42ppts，稅後EPS為2.77元。隨低軌衛星產業即將商業運轉進入高速部署期，將帶動低軌衛星雷
射通訊產品出貨量增加，3Q26營收季增1.4%至3.4億元，預估稅後EPS為2.65元。 
Aleddra Inc.提出訴訟保護應急照明系列產品相關專利： Aleddra Inc.原為萊德光電2008年成立之智慧照明事業
部，公司於2015年將其獨立分割成子公司，主要產品為智慧照明，近期則往光療領域轉型。Aleddra Inc.擁有超過
100項發明專利，目前營收最大的產品為應急照明燈，公司透過發明專利切入美國緊急照明燈市場，包括：大型商
場、倉庫、停車場等，由於該系列產品符合美國法規要求且產品可透過手機直接檢測續電池電力與維修狀態，故
為全集團毛利最高之產品，惟過去3~4年遭美商RAB Lighting Inc.⻑期侵權，公司已於2026年7月正式向美國德州
北區聯邦法院提出訴訟要求判決停止侵權並進行損害賠償，預估2026和2027年將支出約188萬和175萬美元之律
師費用，該費用將採逐月認列，對整體獲利影響有限， 由於該訴訟案勝訴機率高且未來有機會透過業務合作方式，
將推升該系列產品營收動能。另外公司目前著重智慧健康照明，利用非侵入式40Hz伽瑪光調節人體生物節律，改
善高齡族群認知功能與失智症之效果，預計相關產品將於4Q26對外銷售。 
低軌衛星即將商業運轉，近年迎獲利爆發期： 低軌衛星透過底部的雷射光通訊終端設備(Laser Communication 
Terminal, LCT)進行衛星間資料傳輸，單顆衛星約需採用3~4個LCT模組，每顆LCT均需光放大器，萊德光電主要提
供光放大器內部之合束器(Pump Combiner)、隔離器(Isolator)及雷射輸出端接頭，而兩大美系低軌衛星營運商皆
為其客戶 。 由於目前衛星通訊頻寬仍受限且尚無法手機直連 ， 故近期發展趨勢為增加單顆衛星上的LCT雷射通訊終
端數量，未來若太空資料中心計畫被採用，LCT模組用量可望提升至6顆，用量倍增，同時提高單顆LCT頻寬與功
率，由於太空對於封裝與散熱規格的要求將更加嚴苛，產品單價與技術門檻亦大幅提升。由於低軌衛星光市場產
業尚未成熟且標準化，故每家公司設計皆不同，公司及早與客戶共同設計並建立標準，由於需具備相關技術且驗
證時間⻑，競爭者難以進入。因應低軌衛星客戶需求，公司持續擴充泰國廠房與生產人力因應。綜上所述，預估
2026/2027年營收年增50%/27.4%至12.8/16.3億元，稅後EPS為10.06/13.48元。

元件製造商，主要產品包含：光纖、光電應用與發光二極體(LED)，其中截至2Q26產品組合可分為衛星雷射通訊
元件(53.3%) 、 高功率光纖雷射元件(19.1%) 、 光通訊被動元件(14.6%) 、 光纖端面檢測儀與光纖元件製造設備(7.5%)、
智慧照明(4.9%)、其他(0.6%)，其中衛星相關營收比重已逾50%。萊德光電-KY以研發創新為核心，透過自有品牌
深耕歐美市場，另外光電產品專注於客製化OEM項目，主要鎖定利基型市場。 
技術應用領域方面：(1)智慧照明與光療：LED照明轉向智慧與醫療應用，為公司毛利率最高領域；(2)光纖雷射：
屬於千瓦級產品，元件通常較光通訊大且散熱為核心技術，應用於切割、焊接、熱處理、3D列印、醫療與LiDAR
遙測；(3)衛星雷射通訊：在真空中散熱與抗輻射、高低溫差為主要挑戰，台廠多為微波通訊，而公司則專注於雷
射通訊，公司能跨入此領域主要仰賴光通訊與光纖雷射技術累積；(4)光纖傳感：應用於海底石油與天然氣探勘，
適用沙漠、深海等極端環境，因環境差異，元件結構需重新設計；(5)熔融拉椎機台：為核心技術，具端泵與側泵
能力，另外公司開發光纖端檢儀，用於檢測光纖雜質。 
產能方面，美國⻄雅圖為集團總部，包含：研發、製造、業務和⼯廠，負責創新、智財權維護、產品定義及程序維
護；臺灣為決策與營運中心，負責資源調配，未來計畫在臺灣設立研發中心；中國深圳廠負責生產製造與⼯程能
力提升。因應地緣政治風險變化與客戶需求，公司積極評估相關擴廠計畫：(1)董事會通過設立泰國廠投資案，預
計2026年底通過認證開始小量生產；(2)美國大力推動「美國製造」政策，公司亦評估在美國本土進行製造的可能
性，最終視生產成本決定何處製造。

部，公司於2015年將其獨立分割成子公司，主要產品為智慧照明，近期則往光療領域轉型。Aleddra Inc.擁有超過
100項發明專利，目前營收最大的產品為應急照明燈，公司透過發明專利切入美國緊急照明燈市場，包括：大型商
場、倉庫、停車場等，由於該系列產品符合美國法規要求且產品可透過手機直接檢測續電池電力與維修狀態，故
為全集團毛利最高之產品，惟過去3~4年遭美商RAB Lighting Inc.⻑期侵權，公司已於2026年7月正式向美國德州
北區聯邦法院提出訴訟要求判決停止侵權並進行損害賠償，預估2026和2027年將支出約188萬和175萬美元之律
師費用，該費用將採逐月認列，對整體獲利影響有限， 由於該訴訟案勝訴機率高且未來有機會透過業務合作方式，
將推升該系列產品營收動能。另外公司目前著重智慧健康照明，利用非侵入式40Hz伽瑪光調節人體生物節律，改
善高齡族群認知功能與失智症之效果，預計相關產品將於4Q26對外銷售。
低軌衛星即將商業運轉，近年迎獲利爆發期： 低軌衛星透過底部的雷射光通訊終端設備(Laser Communication
Terminal, LCT)進行衛星間資料傳輸，單顆衛星約需採用3~4個LCT模組，每顆LCT均需光放大器，萊德光電主要提
供光放大器內部之合束器(Pump Combiner)、隔離器(Isolator)及雷射輸出端接頭，而兩大美系低軌衛星營運商皆
為其客戶 。 由於目前衛星通訊頻寬仍受限且尚無法手機直連 ， 故近期發展趨勢為增加單顆衛星上的LCT雷射通訊終
端數量，未來若太空資料中心計畫被採用，LCT模組用量可望提升至6顆，用量倍增，同時提高單顆LCT頻寬與功
率，由於太空對於封裝與散熱規格的要求將更加嚴苛，產品單價與技術門檻亦大幅提升。由於低軌衛星光市場產
業尚未成熟且標準化，故每家公司設計皆不同，公司及早與客戶共同設計並建立標準，由於需具備相關技術且驗
證時間⻑，競爭者難以進入。因應低軌衛星客戶需求，公司持續擴充泰國廠房與生產人力因應。綜上所述，預估
2026/2027年營收年增50%/27.4%至12.8/16.3億元，稅後EPS為10.06/13.48元。

萊德光電-KY成立於1999年，總部位於美國⻄雅圖，員⼯人數193人，實收資本額2.47億元，為全球領先光纖被動
元件製造商，主要產品包含：光纖、光電應用與發光二極體(LED)，其中截至2Q26產品組合可分為衛星雷射通訊
元件(53.3%) 、 高功率光纖雷射元件(19.1%) 、 光通訊被動元件(14.6%) 、 光纖端面檢測儀與光纖元件製造設備(7.5%)、
智慧照明(4.9%)、其他(0.6%)，其中衛星相關營收比重已逾50%。萊德光電-KY以研發創新為核心，透過自有品牌
深耕歐美市場，另外光電產品專注於客製化OEM項目，主要鎖定利基型市場。
技術應用領域方面：(1)智慧照明與光療：LED照明轉向智慧與醫療應用，為公司毛利率最高領域；(2)光纖雷射：
屬於千瓦級產品，元件通常較光通訊大且散熱為核心技術，應用於切割、焊接、熱處理、3D列印、醫療與LiDAR
遙測；(3)衛星雷射通訊：在真空中散熱與抗輻射、高低溫差為主要挑戰，台廠多為微波通訊，而公司則專注於雷
射通訊，公司能跨入此領域主要仰賴光通訊與光纖雷射技術累積；(4)光纖傳感：應用於海底石油與天然氣探勘，
適用沙漠、深海等極端環境，因環境差異，元件結構需重新設計；(5)熔融拉椎機台：為核心技術，具端泵與側泵
能力，另外公司開發光纖端檢儀，用於檢測光纖雜質。
產能方面，美國⻄雅圖為集團總部，包含：研發、製造、業務和⼯廠，負責創新、智財權維護、產品定義及程序維
護；臺灣為決策與營運中心，負責資源調配，未來計畫在臺灣設立研發中心；中國深圳廠負責生產製造與⼯程能
力提升。因應地緣政治風險變化與客戶需求，公司積極評估相關擴廠計畫：(1)董事會通過設立泰國廠投資案，預
計2026年底通過認證開始小量生產；(2)美國大力推動「美國製造」政策，公司亦評估在美國本土進行製造的可能
性，最終視生產成本決定何處製造。

items.story: MS OCP 觀察:CPO 搭載 64 顆 XPU 機櫃展示光學 Scale-up 潛力,每通道 200G 電傳輸接近物理極限,但可插拔在 Scale-out 仍維持出貨量領先;封裝良率、光纖對準、可靠性仍是商業化挑戰。聯發科:客製 ASIC 逼近光罩 10 倍,3.5D 較 2.5D 晶粒間能效約 10 倍,3-5 年採用率提高。SK hynix MARS 共享 KV cache 使首 token 時間改善 3-5 倍;HBF 頻寬約 HBM 一半、容量 14 倍,2028 年初送樣。電力散熱為下一個系統瓶頸(6kW cold plate、垂直供電、800V DC)。

items.full_text:
【Raw_Inbox row21394】
(emoji)MS_OCP
 
(emoji)CPO技術逐步接近實際應用，搭載CPO的64顆XPU運算機櫃展示了加速器之間直接採用光學連結的潛力。隨著每通道200G的電氣傳輸逐漸接近物理極限，光學Scale-up的重要性將持續提升，尤其適用於客製化XPU。不過，基於維護便利性及成本優勢，可插拔光學元件仍可望在Scale-out市場維持出貨量領先地位，而封裝良率、光纖對準及可靠性仍是商業化的主要挑戰。
 
(emoji)聯發科指出，客製化ASIC設計正逐步接近光罩尺寸10倍的規模，並認為3.5D整合技術相較傳統2.5D互連，可望將晶粒間能源效率提升約10倍，預期未來3至5年採用率將持續提高。此外，聯發科也強調客製化HBM、專有晶粒間互連技術及設計技術協同最佳化的重要性。隨著系統複雜度不斷提升，先進封裝與客製化ASIC設計服務將迎來結構性成長機會。
 
(emoji)SK hynix推出MARS分離式記憶體架構，透過共享KV快取，避免重複運算，使首次生成Token所需時間改善3至5倍。另一方面，HBF的目標頻寬約為HBM的一半，但容量可達14倍，預計於2028年初提供樣品。隨著推論工作負載持續成長，市場將更加需要整合HBM、DRAM及NAND的異質記憶體架構，並有望帶動傳統GPU搭載HBM以外的記憶體需求擴大。
 
(emoji)電力與散熱正成為下一階段的系統級瓶頸。相關展示包括6kW級cold plates、垂直供電架構及先進微通道散熱技術，反映高效能運算系統面臨日益嚴峻的散熱挑戰。轉向800V直流供電有助於降低電力轉換損耗並提升功率密度。同時，AMD的Helios代理式AI機櫃架構也顯示，隨著GPU基礎設施擴張，CPU需求仍有望同步增加。整體而言，電力傳輸、先進散熱及系統整合能力將成為日益重要的競爭差異化關鍵。

耕興 (6146 TT)  Buy 
 
耕興評價已修正，有機會受惠轉單效應，給 Buy 的投資建
議。  
投資建議 ：美國 FCC 有機率禁止，銷往美國的電子產品在中國
實驗室進行測試，耕興有望接受大量轉單，給 Buy 的投資建議。  
公司簡介： 耕興主要從事電子產品之電磁相容 (EMC) 認證、安規
檢測服務、無線網通認證、手機認證、數位電視認證及防磁零
組件之銷售，全球知名的手機、平板電腦與 NB 業者、晶片廠、
網通廠等多為耕興的客戶。  
耕興的 5G 產品、高階網通的檢測市佔率全球第一： FCC 公布
1H26 的 5G 產品、高階網通檢測的耕興市佔率，分別為 23.97% 、
47.3% ，皆為全球第一。  
FCC 將投票決定中國實驗室未來的商機 ： 路透社 (Reuters) 報導 ，
FCC 將於 10/29/2026 投票表決，來決定賣到美國的電子產品，
是否要禁止在中國實驗室 (非 MRA 國家 )進行測試 ， 若表決通過 ，
預計將於 12/2028 開始生效。  
若 FCC 表決通過，對耕興有利： 耕興具備 FCC 的 MRA 資格，
若 FCC 禁止中國實驗室 ， 將會有大量相關訂單轉移至台灣廠商 ，
耕興檢測產能為全球第一，將直接受惠轉單效應。

2 群益投顧 
  ESG ：  
Environmental ：與 2021 年相比， 2022 年之用電度數較 2021 年減少 0.68% 、
減紙 42%( 減碳 7.92 公噸 CO 2 )。未來規劃：華亞實驗室建置太陽能發電系
統；建置雨水或空調冷凝水回收系統；分階段換發 LED 節能燈具、省電空
調；並於馬達設備增設變頻器以節省用電。  
Social ：體恤員工與資助社團法人嘉義縣扶緣服務協會、新港文教基金會、
與新港奉天宮之金虎爺慢跑活動。國內交易量一百萬元以上的供應商中，
92% 已簽屬「供應商社會責任承諾書」並定期查核；零件部跟生產相關的原
料供應商皆已簽署「不使用衝突礦產聲明書」。  
Governance ：董事會治理制度包含「董事會議事規範」、衡量績效目標落實
之「董事績效評估辦法」、確保誠信經營之「誠信經營守則」、避免貪腐與
符合公平交易法之「誠信經營作業程序及行為指南」等。訂定「資訊安全政
策規範」並以 PDCA (Plan, Do, Check, Act) 循環方式管理。  
公司簡介：  
耕興成立於 1997 年，主要從事電子產品之電磁相容 (EMC) 認證、安規檢測
服務、無線網通認證、手機認證、數位電視認證及防磁零組件之銷售，全球
知名的手機、平板電腦與 NB 業者、晶片廠、網通廠等多為耕興的客戶。  
由於耕興具備 GCF 、 PTCRB 組織的符合性檢測認證，以及加拿大與日本發
證權，只要客戶通過公司認證後即可銷往多國，可降低檢驗所需時間與成
本。  
根據 2022 年 FCC 所公布的資料，耕興在 5G/Wi-Fi 的檢測市占率已經是世
界第一，產能也是全球第一。手機 /網通賣的款式越多，對耕興越有利，單
一產品的出貨量對耕興營收無關。  
台灣無線通訊檢測相關同業包含東研信超 (6840 TT) 、穩得 (6761 TT) 和敦吉
(2459 TT) ，耕興的策略是不斷地去投入比同業多的 CAPEX ，做最先進規格
的檢測，像是毫米波、 Wi-Fi 7 的檢測，以提升營收與獲利。  
營收占比 _地區別：  
浩興為耕興的中國子公司。

AI 筆電、企業級 AP 檢測需求帶動耕興 1H26 營運成長：  
耕興表示， 1H26 獲利增長主要來自於實體 AI 終端裝置發展同時結合非
MRA(Mutual Recognition Arrangement ，相互承認協議 ) 國家地區 FCC 
PAG(Pre-Approval Guidance) 轉單效應帶動大量高階機種檢測需求。  
耕興內部統計最顯著增長的兩大產業族群來自於 AI 筆電及北美企業級 AP
檢測訂單需求增加。  
2H26 營運有望逐季成長：  
展望 2H26 同樣伴隨 PAG 轉單效應持續消化大量湧入的 AI 筆電及北美企業
級 AP 檢測訂單。檢測需求帶動下， 3Q26 獲利表現將有機會比 2Q26 強勁，
同時 4Q26 的獲利也有機會更上一層樓， 4Q26 是 2027 年高階旗艦級手機種
換機潮的檢測高峰期。  
耕興的 5G 產品、高階網通的檢測市佔率全球第一：  
FCC 公布 1H26 的 5G 產品、高階網通檢測的耕興市佔率，分別為 23.97% 、
47.3% ，皆為全球第一。

子產品，是否要禁止在中國實驗室 (非 MRA 國家 )進行測試，若表決通過，
預計將於 12/2028 開始生效。  
FCC 主席表示， 2025 年賣到美國的電子產品，約有 82% 是在中國實驗室進
行測試，而在美國實驗室測試的比例不到 4%。  
若 FCC 表決通過，對耕興有利：  
耕興具備 FCC 的 MRA 資格，若 FCC 禁止中國實驗室，將會有大量相關訂
單轉移至台灣廠商，耕興檢測產能為全球第一，將直接受惠轉單效應。

  【投資評等調整機制】  
  投資評等係「首次」給予特定個股投資評等時，其前一日收盤價相較 3 個月
目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為四個等級，定義如上。
爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。   
「強力買進」、「買進」及「區間操作」均有 upside 目標價。差別僅在於，
首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。  
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，
就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基本面及
股價變化，直到停止推薦。  
停止推薦情境：

目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為四個等級，定義如上。
爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。
「強力買進」、「買進」及「區間操作」均有 upside 目標價。差別僅在於，
首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，
就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基本面及
股價變化，直到停止推薦。
停止推薦情境：
1.  達目標價。
2.  雖未達原訂目標價，但檢視基本面、訊息面、籌碼面等多方訊息，研
判股價上漲空間已然有限，將適時出具降評報告。
3.  推薦後股價不漲反跌。

  【免責聲明】

投資人於買賣證券、選擇權、期貨或其他證券相關之衍生性商品提供詢價服

TrendForce：2027年CSP資本支出破1.5兆美元，AI Server產值年增逾90%

根據TrendForce最新AI server產業研究，全球前九大CSP（Google、Amazon、Meta、Microsoft、Oracle，以及ByteDance、Tencent、Alibaba、Baidu）持續擴大server及AI基礎設施投資。

資本支出預估  
- 2026年：前九大CSP資本支出總額逾9,570億美元，年增106%。  
- 2027年：有望突破1.5兆美元，年增60%（較先前預估的50%上調）。  
上調主因包括：server整機價格上漲、零組件缺貨推高報價，以及供應商要求預付款導致CSP需提早現金支出。

AI Server出貨與產值
在CSP投資力道不減下，AI server拉貨需求增溫。除超大型CSP外，Tesla、CoreWeave等Tier-2業者亦持續採購；再加上Neocloud、主權型AI專案與大型語言模型業者新模型／應用推出，出貨動能強勁。  

- 2026年AI server出貨年增32.2%；2027年再年增近36%。  
- 產值方面：2026年AI server約4,790億美元，占整體server（含通用＋AI）約6,392億美元的近75%。  
- 2027年因終端訂單以NVIDIA GB300、VR200及AMD Helios等整櫃式方案為主，加上記憶體等關鍵零組件短缺推升新世代機櫃ASP，整體server產值將首度跨越1兆美元；AI server產值躍升至近9,200億美元，年增逾90%，占比提高至約81%。
